skill.name: replicate-handler
skill.description: Use Replicate AI models with TypeScript examples for quick runs, long jobs, and SDK type references.
skill.summary: Guides Replicate SDK setup, model execution, polling, and TypeScript integration.
skill.author: AayushBaniya2006

security_audit.summary: The audited files are a Replicate SDK usage guide and a TypeScript type reference. The static command, network, and sensitive-file alerts are explained by Markdown formatting, TypeScript syntax, or intended SDK authentication. No evidence of malware, prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or system reconnaissance was found.

remediation.suggestion: Add a warning to keep REPLICATE_API_TOKEN out of source control and rotate exposed tokens.

remediation.issue: Package installation is shown without version guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend installing a pinned Replicate SDK version and reviewing dependency changes before use.

remediation.issue: Long-running model polling can create cost or resource risks.
remediation.suggestion: Advise timeouts, cancellation paths, and usage limits for expensive predictions.

content.value_statement: Replicate integrations can be unclear when jobs finish at different speeds. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical patterns for quick runs, polling, and typed responses.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install the Replicate SDK and configure REPLICATE_API_TOKEN.
Provides a quick run pattern for short Replicate model jobs.
Provides an Inngest polling pattern for long-running predictions.
Includes TypeScript references for predictions, streams, trainings, and webhooks.
Shows failure handling when Replicate returns a failed prediction status.
limitations: Does not include a complete application or runnable project scaffold.
Requires a valid Replicate account and API token.
Does not choose model versions or manage model costs for users.
Type references may lag behind newer Replicate SDK releases.

best_practices: Store REPLICATE_API_TOKEN outside source control and rotate it if exposed.
Use quick runs only for jobs that complete within request time limits.
Poll long-running predictions with durable steps and clear failure handling.
anti_patterns: Do not paste Replicate tokens into prompts, logs, or source files.
Do not run expensive models without rate limits or user confirmation.
Do not poll inside a busy loop or block server resources.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents integrate the Replicate SDK, run models, poll predictions, and understand TypeScript response shapes.

faq.question: Does it run Replicate models by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that an agent can adapt inside your project.

faq.question: Which API token does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects a Replicate API token stored as REPLICATE_API_TOKEN in your environment.

faq.question: When should I use polling?
faq.answer: Use polling for video generation, large models, or any prediction that may outlive one request.

faq.question: Does it include webhook guidance?
faq.answer: The reference file includes webhook-related SDK types and validation function signatures.

faq.question: Can it help with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The content is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
